title: Introduce operator-endorsement rbacv2 + region-pin assertor and access-provenance bridge
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds operator-endorsement RBAC assertions, a lightweight region-pin assertor middleware, KMS-consent cache hooks, and an access-provenance audit bridge. Backwards-compatible rollout behind feature flag; no API changes.
description:
Summary: This PR adds an 'operator endorsement' layer to RBAC v2 that lets operator-scoped actions require an endorsement token (short-lived attestation) before sensitive KMS operations or cross-region resource bindings proceed. It also introduces a region-pin assertor middleware that canonicalizes claimed region headers and produces a provenance token consumed by downstream KMS-routing, and an access-provenance bridge that ties RBAC decisions to audit entries for traceable post-hoc review.
Motivation: We observed ambiguity when operator sessions performed elevated actions across tenants/regions which made post-incident forensics difficult. Existing RBACv2 allowed operator roles but lacked an endorsement handshake and a standard provenance artifact to correlate with KMS usage and audit logs. This PR aims to reduce blast radius, make policy decisions auditable, and enable conservative rollouts of region-pin enforcement.
Design highlights:
- operator endorsement: a new claim on operator sessions (endorsement_id) that must be presented when the scope crosses a guarded resource. Endorsements are minted by the operator-endorser service after policy checks and MFA confirmation; the runtime validates the endorsement signature and TTL.
- region-pin assertor middleware: intercepts inbound requests, normalizes region headers (X-Redwood-Claimed-Region), looks up tenant residency policy, emits X-Redwood-Region-Proof token (HMACed with service key) and attaches a human-readable reason in X-Redwood-Region-Note for observability.
- KMS-consent cache hooks: runtime now consults a small in-memory consent cache (LRU) to short-circuit repeated consent checks for the same (tenant, operator, key) tuple for a configurable window. Misses invoke existing KMS consent flow.
- access-provenance bridge: audit writer now includes a provenance blob (base64 JSON) with rbac_decision, endorsement_id, region_proof, and route_fingerprint. This enables downstream auditors to verify which endorsement authorized an operation and which KMS key owner saw the request.
Rollout plan: guarded behind feature flag security.operator_endorsement.enabled defaulting to off. Initial rollout will enable generation and validation only in staging, with read-only provenance in production before enforcing denies.

Review conversation summary:
- Liam O'Connor: "High level: good separation of concerns. Two asks: (1) add an opt-out for tenants on provenance collection (privacy/legal), and (2) confirm KMS consent cache TTL defaults and observable evictions."
- Maya Patel (author): "Addressed both: added tenant_provenance_collection opt-in in tenant config (default true), and set consent cache TTL to 5m with configurable env var REDWOOD_CONSENT_CACHE_TTL. Added eviction metrics and tests."
- Elena Ruiz: "Please add a short circuit that returns 400 instead of 500 for malformed endorsements; otherwise lgtm."
- Maya Patel: "Changed validation to return 400 and added unit tests covering malformed endorsements and replay attempts."
- Chao Wang: "Suggest to log provenance blob only at INFO for operator events and redact sensitive KMS key ids in the blob. Also asked to run perf canary."
- Maya Patel: "Redaction implemented for key ids (keep fingerprint only). Perf canary job was added and passed with a 3% median latency overhead in the staging profile."
CI status: initial CI failed on lint (max-line-length in docs), fixed in follow-up commit. Unit tests pass, e2e smoke passed in staging. Perf canary: staging median latency +3%, p95 +7% — within SLO for non-enforced rollout.
Security review: security-runbook noted change; SRE requested an alert for consent_cache_miss_rate spike.
Merge outcome: merged to main via squash on 2026-02-25 after approvals from Liam and Elena; merge commit message includes summary and Linear links.
Notes for operators:
- Feature flag security.operator_endorsement.enabled must be toggled in console for production enforcement.
- Tenant opt-in for provenance configured via tenant API (tenant.provenance.enabled).
- Watch metrics: security_endorsement_validation_failures, consent_cache_hit_ratio, audit_provenance_size_bytes.
Backwards compatibility: The added headers are optional and systems that do not understand them will be ignored; provenance blob writing is opt-in per tenant and does not change public API shapes.
Follow-ups tracked: ENG-3301 implement operator-endorser service autoscaling and HSM-backed signing; ENG-3310 policy-sim tests for large tenant rolls.
